database_summary: Relational academic scheduling database (SQLite) containing descriptive tables for buildings, departments, categories, majors, staff/faculty, classrooms and subjects, plus event/assignment-like tables for classes, faculty teaching assignments, faculty subject proficiencies, student schedules and class-status codes. Many tables model current state or descriptive attributes; Classes and Student_Schedules represent scheduled events/assignments (history/events). Foreign keys link classes to subjects and rooms, staff to faculty-related tables, and categories to subjects and faculty categories.

accepted.name: classes_with_room_and_building
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Classes.ClassID,
  Classes.SubjectID,
  Classes.ClassRoomID,
  Classes.Credits,
  Classes.StartDate,
  Classes.StartTime,
  Classes.Duration,
  Classes.MondaySchedule,
  Classes.TuesdaySchedule,
  Classes.WednesdaySchedule,
  Classes.ThursdaySchedule,
  Classes.FridaySchedule,
  Classes.SaturdaySchedule,
  Class_Rooms.BuildingCode,
  Class_Rooms.PhoneAvailable,
  Buildings.BuildingName,
  Buildings.NumberOfFloors,
  Buildings.ElevatorAccess,
  Buildings.SiteParkingAvailable
FROM Classes
LEFT JOIN Class_Rooms ON Classes.ClassRoomID = Class_Rooms.ClassRoomID
LEFT JOIN Buildings ON Class_Rooms.BuildingCode = Buildings.BuildingCode
accepted.description: Denormalized one-row-per-class offering with classroom and building attributes. Useful when analyzing where classes are held, room facilities, or joining to faculty/students by ClassID. | Use for: List classes with room/building info; Which buildings host the most classes; Find classes in rooms without phone or without elevator access; Join to Faculty_Classes or Student_Schedules for attendance/roster-level queries

accepted.name: class_schedule_weekday_flags
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ClassID,
  SubjectID,
  ClassRoomID,
  Credits,
  StartDate,
  StartTime,
  Duration,
  MondaySchedule,
  TuesdaySchedule,
  WednesdaySchedule,
  ThursdaySchedule,
  FridaySchedule,
  SaturdaySchedule,
  (CASE WHEN MondaySchedule = 1 THEN 'Mon' ELSE '' END) ||
  (CASE WHEN TuesdaySchedule = 1 THEN (CASE WHEN MondaySchedule = 1 THEN ',' ELSE '' END) || 'Tue' ELSE '' END) ||
  (CASE WHEN WednesdaySchedule = 1 THEN (CASE WHEN MondaySchedule = 1 OR TuesdaySchedule = 1 THEN ',' ELSE '' END) || 'Wed' ELSE '' END) ||
  (CASE WHEN ThursdaySchedule = 1 THEN (CASE WHEN MondaySchedule = 1 OR TuesdaySchedule = 1 OR WednesdaySchedule = 1 THEN ',' ELSE '' END) || 'Thu' ELSE '' END) ||
  (CASE WHEN FridaySchedule = 1 THEN (CASE WHEN MondaySchedule = 1 OR TuesdaySchedule = 1 OR WednesdaySchedule = 1 OR ThursdaySchedule = 1 THEN ',' ELSE '' END) || 'Fri' ELSE '' END) ||
  (CASE WHEN SaturdaySchedule = 1 THEN (CASE WHEN MondaySchedule = 1 OR TuesdaySchedule = 1 OR WednesdaySchedule = 1 OR ThursdaySchedule = 1 OR FridaySchedule = 1 THEN ',' ELSE '' END) || 'Sat' ELSE '' END) AS scheduled_weekdays
FROM Classes
accepted.description: Normalized weekly schedule flags per class with a derived descriptive column listing scheduled weekdays. Useful for filtering or grouping classes by meeting days or computing daily loads. | Use for: Find classes meeting on a particular weekday; Aggregate class counts by weekday; Filter classes that meet multiple specific weekdays

accepted.name: faculty_full_profile
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Staff.StaffID,
  Staff.StfFirstName,
  Staff.StfLastname,
  Staff.StfStreetAddress,
  Staff.StfCity,
  Staff.StfState,
  Staff.StfZipCode,
  Staff.StfAreaCode,
  Staff.StfPhoneNumber,
  Staff.Salary,
  Staff.DateHired,
  Staff.Position,
  Faculty.Title,
  Faculty.Status,
  Faculty.Tenured,
  Departments.DepartmentID AS DepartmentID,
  Departments.DeptName AS DeptName,
  Departments.DeptChair AS DeptChair
FROM Staff
LEFT JOIN Faculty ON Staff.StaffID = Faculty.StaffID
LEFT JOIN Departments ON Staff.StaffID = Departments.DeptChair
accepted.description: One row per faculty person combining Staff and Faculty attributes and department chair status. Useful for analyses of faculty salaries, tenure, and contact details. | Use for: List faculty with salary and tenure info; Find department chairs and their contact/salary details; Join faculty to Faculty_Classes or Faculty_Subjects for teaching/proficiency analyses

accepted.name: faculty_subject_proficiency
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  SubjectID,
  COUNT(StaffID) AS faculty_count,
  AVG(ProficiencyRating) AS avg_ProficiencyRating,
  MIN(ProficiencyRating) AS min_ProficiencyRating,
  MAX(ProficiencyRating) AS max_ProficiencyRating
FROM Faculty_Subjects
GROUP BY SubjectID
accepted.description: Aggregated proficiency metrics per subject: average, min, max ProficiencyRating and count of faculty with a rating. Useful for measuring subject coverage and identifying subjects with few instructors. | Use for: Which subjects have the most/least faculty proficiency; Average proficiency rating by subject; Identify subjects lacking proficient instructors

accepted.name: student_enrollments_with_status
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Student_Schedules.StudentID,
  Student_Schedules.ClassID,
  Student_Schedules.ClassStatus,
  Student_Schedules.Grade,
  Student_Class_Status.ClassStatusDescription,
  Students.StudFirstName,
  Students.StudLastName,
  Students.StudMajor,
  Students.StudGPA
FROM Student_Schedules
LEFT JOIN Student_Class_Status ON Student_Schedules.ClassStatus = Student_Class_Status.ClassStatus
LEFT JOIN Students ON Student_Schedules.StudentID = Students.StudentID
accepted.description: One row per student-class enrollment with class status description and student basic info. Useful for grade/reporting, enrollment counts, and status-based cohorts (e.g., completed vs enrolled). | Use for: List student grades with human-readable status; Count enrolled vs completed by class; Join to Classes or Subjects for performance by course

accepted.name: subject_category_with_department
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Subjects.SubjectID,
  Subjects.CategoryID,
  Subjects.SubjectCode,
  Subjects.SubjectName,
  Subjects.SubjectPreReq,
  Subjects.SubjectDescription,
  Categories.CategoryDescription,
  Categories.DepartmentID
FROM Subjects
LEFT JOIN Categories ON Subjects.CategoryID = Categories.CategoryID
accepted.description: One row per Subject including its Category and the Category's Department. Useful when analyzing subjects by department or category-level aggregations. | Use for: Group subjects by department; Find all subjects in a category; Join to Classes to get course offerings with department context

accepted.name: faculty_teaching_load
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Faculty_Classes.StaffID,
  COUNT(Faculty_Classes.ClassID) AS classes_taught,
  SUM(Classes.Credits) AS total_credits_taught
FROM Faculty_Classes
LEFT JOIN Classes ON Faculty_Classes.ClassID = Classes.ClassID
GROUP BY Faculty_Classes.StaffID
accepted.description: Counts of classes taught per faculty member and total credits taught. Useful for workload and distribution analyses. Grain: one row per StaffID (faculty). | Use for: Who teaches the most classes or credits; Compare teaching load across faculty; Identify faculty with no class assignments (outer join with Faculty)

accepted.name: students_with_major_and_gpa
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Students.StudentID,
  Students.StudFirstName,
  Students.StudLastName,
  Students.StudStreetAddress,
  Students.StudCity,
  Students.StudState,
  Students.StudZipCode,
  Students.StudAreaCode,
  Students.StudPhoneNumber,
  Students.StudGPA,
  Students.StudMajor,
  Majors.Major AS Major
FROM Students
LEFT JOIN Majors ON Students.StudMajor = Majors.MajorID
accepted.description: Student dimension projection with major text and a normalized GPA flag indicating low/high (derived continuous); keep raw StudGPA and MajorID for joins. Useful for student cohort selection by GPA or major. | Use for: Select students by major or GPA; Join students to enrollments and classes for performance analysis; Compute counts or averages of GPA by major

accepted.name: top_faculty_by_proficiency_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  StaffID,
  SubjectID,
  ProficiencyRating,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY SubjectID ORDER BY ProficiencyRating DESC) AS prof_rank
FROM Faculty_Subjects
accepted.description: Per-subject ranking of faculty by ProficiencyRating exposing subject-level rank. Useful as a reusable top-K building block (filter WHERE prof_rank <= K downstream). | Use for: Get top N faculty per subject by proficiency; Identify faculty who are highest-rated for a subject
